## Natural history notes

A small sweat bee characterized by its brilliant metallic green body, slender build, and relatively sparse hairs compared with many larger bees. In Florida, it is found in gardens, forest edges, hammocks, parks, fields, and other habitats with flowering plants and nearby nesting material. Adults visit flowers for nectar and pollen, while females nest in soft, decaying wood or rotting logs, creating small brood cells for their young and contributing to pollination in wooded and semi-open habitats.
